integrity.on_failure: load integrity evidence and canonical sources; do not trust compact routing

recursive_context.on_failure: stop compact interpretation, load the named canonical owner when safe, and report index drift; never load the complete contour by default

terms.definition: Inspect, modify, commit, publish, and live-external actions are separate authorization phases for the current logical task. A completed, redirected, ambiguous, discussion-only, or analysis-only request does not authorize a later state-changing phase.

Use the target-registered canonical owner for a fact type, preserve its conflict resolver and synchronization direction, and treat routing records, summaries, evidence, frequency, and recency as non-authoritative unless that owner says otherwise.

Classify risk from changed facts, affected boundaries, reversibility, external effects, and target policy rather than from file count or apparent patch size; expand to the applicable owner, approval, safety, and validation evidence before acting.

A change that crosses a target-recorded protected category requires a current scoped approval whose semantic and path surfaces cover the actual change; changing the plan or scope invalidates approval as defined by the target policy.

Name changed semantic facts, re-derive their invariants, identify canonical owners and directly dependent surfaces, reconcile related findings as one repair set, validate the result, and report unresolved relationships and residual risk.

Start from the smallest matching profile and selected index branch. Expand only for an applicable owner, safety or approval boundary, named dependency, changed-fact relationship, conflict, failed validation, or explicit broader audit, and record why the expansion occurred.

semantic_preload.fallback: load the referenced canonical owner and do not infer a missing stale conflicting cyclic or unsupported compact term

known_gaps: The target contains no implementation brief, product source, package metadata, tests, CI, or project validation commands.
Named human owner identities are not available; repository-maintainer roles are used.
The workspace exposes no usable Git revision, so installation evidence cannot be revision-bound until the repository has a commit.
Codex loading is configured through AGENTS.md but has not been independently observed in a later session.
Runtime, input/output contract, provider requirements, delivery format, and deployment expectations are not established.

Optional modules other than AI infrastructure, architecture knowledge, blueprint change, Debug Mode, effectiveness metrics, installed operations, multi-assistant bridges, and subagent delegation remain deferred until target evidence justifies them.
expansion_policy: load required safety and owner evidence, record expansion reason, measured context, and intentionally omitted context
